answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake that grows with reputation, so creating fake identities has a real cost. When one bad actor is caught, the penalty does not stop at that account: it sends a ripple through its linked identities, freezing their stakes as well. Like a marble rolling down a spiral track, each new identity must pay more the faster it is created, so mass-producing fakes becomes exponentially expensive while honest agents pay almost nothing.
